describes: A coping slab of split slate across the top of a dry wall (port step 2b, R2a; the design's SN2, SN4 and SN9): a rigid block on its bed, its top and bed the laminae's planes, its long sides and ends split, one plane each; as wide as the wall's top and its overhangs, its front a seeded few mm proud of the stair's face. An open end (where its run ends over a riser) is drawn whole and may be knocked at its top corners; a joint end is set in by its half joint and drawn where the joint is seen. L0 chamfers the top's arrises, its perimeter, and only those: the bed's would face down (SN7), each end's upright arrises would make corners where three chamfers meet in a point too fine to draw (SN8), and a knock is a break after the dressing, its arrises sharp.
note: Sizes from R1's walling table (packs/stavanger-1989/walling.json, the dry-split-1874 working) and its laying: w a coping's cell (copeLeastMm 200 where a run leaves less than a slab, to copeLengthMm's 1000) less a half joint (2 to 6 mm) at each joint end; h its run's thickness (copeThickMm 70 to 100) less its bed's half joint; d the wall's top (wall.py's 420 mm) and its overhangs (50 mm on a standing wall). Levels: the design's SN8 budgets per piece (120 and 48); L1's error is L0's chamfers' (their sagitta, 8.5 mm at a 12 mm leg; up to 9.8 mm measured at a corner where two meet), 11 mm as the step's, against kinds/wall.json's 4 (blender.md, the conflicts); L2 to L4 are the chunk's. The part's own numbers (chamfer, which arrises it takes, chips, patch sets) are stones.py's PARAMS until this schema takes a params object (reviews/lt1/port/2b/r2a/stones/blender.md).
